scope: Word table fidelity: forced line breaks inside table cells (w:br) rendered as real lines, plus a Word-COM probe of per-row heights that explains the rowFlowScale fudge

reference.wordPage72: Word export of page 72 via Word COM ExportAsFixedFormat (web/.tmp/word-page72.pdf, screenshot web/.tmp/word-page72b.png): 6 equal columns, body starts with the tail of a row split from page 71, and the w:tblHeader row is repeated at the top of every page
reference.breaks: document.xml: 738 w:br, 733 of them plain line breaks inside 579 table cells (mostly '+' bullet lists in the 'Nội dung' column); body/hyperlink text uses the same marker
reference.rowCounts: big table = 839 rows / 5034 cells / 4186 w:noWrap / 680 plain w:br / all rows w:trHeight 227 atLeast / tblLayout fixed
reference.rowPositions: Word COM Cell(i,1).Range start -> Information(6) page-Y and Information(3) page for all 839 rows (web/.tmp/word-row-positions.json); table spans Word pages 71-496, 424 pages

changes.tableCellBreaks: `.op-word-table p { white-space: pre-wrap }` in web/src/styles.css. parseRun already turned w:br into '\n', but table cell paragraphs were the only Word text surface without pre-wrap, so 733 breaks collapsed into spaces and each bullet list inside a cell rendered as one joined line. Body paragraphs (.op-word-p) already had pre-wrap.
changes.rowFlowScale: default rowFlowScale 1.417 -> 1.4125 after the break change, keeping 546 pages (web/src/app/office-webapp.component.ts)

probes.rowsHeightApi: Word Rows.Height returns the w:trHeight minimum (11.35pt) for all 839 rows, not the laid-out height; Cell.Range.ComputeStatistics(wdStatisticLines) returns 0 for table cell ranges, so Word's per-cell line counts cannot be read directly (recorded unknown unk_8c68b89f715850f5 is still open).
probes.rowHeightsFromY: Consecutive row starts on the same page give an exact row height. 415 of 838 pairs are same-page: total-word/our-DOM ratio 0.95, i.e. our natural row heights are within 5% of Word for rows that fit on one page. Page-crossing pairs carry the repeated header row, so their deltas overstate Word's row height (this inflated an earlier estimate to 1.37x).
probes.repeatedHeader: Rendering the repeated w:tblHeader row (tested in build 630): 664 pages at rowFlowScale 1.417; rescaling to 543/547 pages gave mean Dice 0.536/0.521 against 0.579 baseline, so the repeat was reverted. The QA page-text reference is extracted from Word's body range and does not contain the repeated header row, so adding it lowers Dice even though Word displays it.
probes.noWrap: 4186/5034 cells carry w:noWrap but the table is tblLayout fixed; Word's page-72 export wraps those cells normally (multi-line descriptions inside 110px columns), so noWrap is not applied to rendering.

verification.dice: qa-page-map mean Dice 0.582, 98/546 pages >= 0.8, best-offset 0.691, 194 pages >= 0.8 at the best of -2..2 (baseline 1.417 + collapsed breaks: 0.579 / 100 / 0.691 / 194)
verification.screenshot: web/.tmp/our-page38-final.png shows the retry bullet list inside the table cell on separate lines; web/.tmp/our-page72-final.png shows the same page as Word's export

remaining: Per-page table-body layout is still approximate: rows that straddle a page boundary start at a different row than in Word, so most of the 424 table pages stay below Dice 0.8. Closing it needs Word's row page-fit (including the repeated header space) and identical line breaking.

Table cells still ignore w:tcPr visuals: header-row fill (w:shd D9D9D9), cell vertical alignment and per-edge borders are not modelled, so the repeated header/header cells look white and top-aligned versus Word's grey centred cells.
